First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062337/assets/6805467a24cb40559f205cbfcecc4f5a34ff2ec6ebda8ae67f997c02f123b53c.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=1\cdot 1=1.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=(-4)\cdot 3-2\cdot 1=-12-2=-14.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,-14\,|\cdot 1 \\  & =14.\end{aligned}
$$
